title: Weekly AI & Agentic Systems Digest — November 15–21, 2026
summary: This week tightened runtime authority: AWS added task-scoped credentials and governed agent purchasing; Bedrock gained a new OpenAI model pair; a Microsoft agent package was compromised; MCP patched another set of trust-boundary failures; and Google separated tool discovery from schema loading.

developments.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI releases 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 were compromised
developments.availability: The malicious wheels were published November 17 and removed from PyPI. Version 1.26.0 is the last known clean release; the advisory lists no patched version.
developments.what_changed: Unauthorized agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 wheels added a .pth startup hook that executed whenever Python started. The payload collected environment variables, credential files, process environments, and cloud or CI tokens and sent the data to an external endpoint.
developments.why_it_matters: An agent dependency became a credential-stealing foothold before application code imported it, crossing CI, developer, container, and cloud-identity boundaries.
developments.platform_impact: Response must cover lockfiles, package caches, internal mirrors, build logs, deployed images, outbound network evidence, and every credential reachable from affected processes. Uninstalling or downgrading does not revoke exposed secrets.
developments.recommended_action: Block both versions and their published hashes, isolate affected systems, search caches and images, and rotate all reachable AWS, Azure, GitHub, CI, package-registry, and application credentials.
developments.watchouts: The packages were removed from public PyPI, but cached wheels and internal mirrors can continue distributing them. No patched release is listed.

developments.title: AWS STS adds runtime-scoped credentials for agents and workloads
developments.availability: Available in all AWS commercial Regions, GovCloud (US), European Sovereign Cloud (Germany), and China Regions.
developments.what_changed: GetScopedCredentials derives credentials from an existing temporary session while reducing permissions, session duration, or both. Derived credentials preserve the caller identity, can be narrowed recursively, and each call is recorded in CloudTrail.
developments.why_it_matters: Parent agents can issue task-specific credentials to subagents without creating or assuming a separate role for every delegation.
developments.platform_impact: Agent authorization can follow the work graph: broad parent sessions can mint short-lived child credentials with smaller action and time boundaries, while CloudTrail retains the delegation chain.
developments.recommended_action: Pilot the API with two subagent tasks and verify denied actions, recursive narrowing, duration limits, identity preservation, and incident reconstruction from CloudTrail.
developments.watchouts: The API only narrows existing temporary credentials. An overprivileged parent session remains a high-value target, and IAM policy still controls who may derive credentials.

developments.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol become generally available on Amazon Bedrock
developments.availability: Available through the Amazon Bedrock console and supported Bedrock APIs; AWS directs customers to Bedrock documentation for Regions, endpoints, features, inference profiles, and pricing.
developments.what_changed: AWS added GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol to Bedrock. AWS positions Astra for difficult reasoning, research, coding, multimodal, and agentic work, including an Ultrafast mode, while Sol targets recurring higher-volume coding and multistep workflows.
developments.why_it_matters: Bedrock teams gain another model pair within existing AWS access-control, governance, and audit boundaries.
developments.platform_impact: Model routers and evaluation suites should treat Astra and Sol as distinct candidates for planner or reviewer stages and scaled execution, with explicit model IDs, fallback behavior, and completed-task economics.
developments.recommended_action: Run 40 frozen tool-use tasks against Astra, Sol, and current defaults, measuring completion, intervention, latency, tokens, and total cost.
developments.watchouts: The announcement does not establish superiority for a specific workload. Region, feature, inference-profile, quota, and pricing support must be verified before rollout.

developments.title: AgentCore payments adds per-request purchasing through AWS Marketplace
developments.availability: Available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore payments is available. The initial AWS Billing integration supports the x402 exact-price scheme for selected Marketplace products.
developments.what_changed: Agents can discover selected x402-enabled APIs, software, data, and content and pay per request in US dollars through the developer's AWS bill. Controls include payment-session budgets, approved sellers, Private Marketplace policy, signed quotes, CloudTrail events, and Cost Explorer visibility.
developments.why_it_matters: Agents can acquire a paid tool at runtime without holding a stablecoin wallet or requiring a separately provisioned seller API key.
developments.platform_impact: Tool acquisition becomes a privileged side effect that needs IAM separation, seller policy, spend limits, billing alerts, agreement tracking, and reconciliation alongside ordinary tool authorization.
developments.recommended_action: Use the sample in a sandbox with a five-cent session budget, separate budget-setting and spending roles, one approved seller, and alerts for every transaction.
developments.watchouts: A first purchase creates an AWS Marketplace agreement and real charges. Catalog coverage is limited to participating sellers and the initial integration supports fixed exact-price requests.

developments.title: MCP reference servers v2.5.0 patch eight additional vulnerabilities
developments.what_changed: The release fixes execution through Git maintenance hooks, lazy fetch, filter and merge drivers, and submodule configuration; out-of-tree index reads; filesystem symlink-swap races; and NAT64-assisted private-address access.
developments.why_it_matters: Repository metadata, filesystem races, and network address translation again crossed supposedly bounded MCP tool surfaces.
developments.platform_impact: Version inventories and regression tests must cover exact server packages, Git behavior, repository-controlled configuration, filesystem semantics, and private-network routing outside the prompt layer.
developments.recommended_action: Install the exact patched versions, then rerun hostile-repository, out-of-tree index, symlink-swap, submodule, and NAT64/private-address tests in an isolated environment.
developments.watchouts: Package managers can rank older calendar-version npm packages above the new semantic versions. The release also documents a remaining Windows listing limitation and an incomplete post-write confinement check.
developments.new_delta: Since the November 14 issue covered v2.4.0 and six vulnerabilities, v2.5.0 fixes eight newly disclosed flaws across Git, filesystem, and network trust boundaries.

developments.title: Gemini API adds on-demand Tool Retrieval for large function and MCP catalogs
developments.availability: Available in preview in the Gemini Interactions API for Gemini 3.6 and later, including Gemini 4 models; no separate feature charge is listed beyond model token billing.
developments.what_changed: Developers can mark function tools or remote MCP servers for deferred loading. The model initially sees names and descriptions, then uses tool_search to load selected parameter schemas only when needed; server-side retrieval remains within one API request, while client-side retrieval supports private registries and permission filters.
developments.why_it_matters: Large tool catalogs no longer require every full schema in every prompt, separating discovery from schema hydration and invocation.
developments.platform_impact: AgentCore Gateway and MCP architectures can adopt the same boundary even without Gemini: search a governed registry, apply permissions, hydrate only selected schemas, and record each stage for audit and debugging.
developments.recommended_action: Compare eager and deferred catalogs with 100 tools on token use, tool-selection accuracy, permission leakage, latency, and trace completeness.
developments.watchouts: The feature is preview. Server-side retrieval exposes tool names and descriptions to the model, while client-side retrieval adds a round trip and leaves authorization correctness to the application.

devops_impacts.text: Inventory agent dependencies by exact version and hash across registries, caches, mirrors, CI, images, and running environments; package removal does not invalidate stolen credentials.
Model agent authority as separate credentials, tool permissions, and spending budgets, with every delegation and purchase reconstructable from durable audit records.
Pin exact MCP packages and Bedrock model identifiers, and test migration and fallback paths because package ordering and managed catalogs can change runtime behavior without an application-code diff.
Separate tool discovery, permission filtering, schema hydration, and execution so a large catalog does not automatically become a large prompt or authority surface.
Measure completed-task economics across model choice, deferred schemas, retries, and paid tool calls; request prices alone do not capture agent workflow cost.

bring_to_work.title: Compromised-package sweep
bring_to_work.what: Search the full software supply chain for the two malicious Agent Framework releases and their published wheel hashes.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct fit for Python agent environments, including services that call Amazon Bedrock or run inside AWS CI and compute.
bring_to_work.next_step: Query SBOMs, lockfiles, caches, mirrors, CI artifacts, and images; isolate hits and rotate every credential reachable from affected processes.

bring_to_work.title: Delegated-credential pilot
bring_to_work.what: Use GetScopedCredentials to give two subagents different task and time boundaries from one parent temporary session.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct AWS fit for AgentCore, containers, Lambda, or custom agent runtimes that delegate work.
bring_to_work.next_step: Test allowed and denied calls, recursive narrowing, expiration, identity preservation, and CloudTrail reconstruction.

bring_to_work.title: Bedrock model cost-per-success evaluation
bring_to_work.what: Compare Astra and Sol with current Bedrock defaults on representative tool-use and coding workflows.
bring_to_work.fit: Direct Bedrock model-routing and fallback evaluation within the existing AWS governance boundary.
bring_to_work.next_step: Freeze 40 tasks and record completion, interventions, latency, token use, total cost, and failure recovery.

bring_to_work.title: Tool-catalog boundary test
bring_to_work.what: Place 100 tools behind a governed searchable registry and compare eager schemas with deferred retrieval.
bring_to_work.fit: Transferable to AgentCore Gateway and MCP even though the reference implementation is Gemini's Interactions API.
bring_to_work.next_step: Measure token use, selection accuracy, permission leakage, latency, and trace completeness for both designs.

watchouts.text: The Agent Framework incident requires credential rotation and forensic review, not only dependency rollback; internal mirrors may continue serving the malicious wheels.

GetScopedCredentials cannot compensate for an excessively privileged parent session, and Marketplace purchasing introduces real agreements and charges that need separate budget-setting and spending identities.
MCP v2.5.0 requires exact package versions and still documents residual limitations; read-only labels remain weaker than process, filesystem, and network isolation.
Gemini Tool Retrieval is preview, while Bedrock model positioning and economics require workload-specific validation of Regions, features, quotas, latency, and cost.

telegram_text:
# Weekly AI & Agentic Systems Digest — November 15–21, 2026

This week’s pattern was tighter runtime authority: AWS added task-scoped credentials and governed agent purchasing; Bedrock gained a new OpenAI model pair; a Microsoft agent package was compromised; MCP patched another set of trust-boundary failures; and Google separated tool discovery from schema loading.

## What changed

**1. Microsoft Agent Framework’s PyPI package was compromised.** *Security incident, November 17–18.* Unauthorized `agent-framework` 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 wheels added a `.pth` startup hook that ran whenever Python started, collected environment variables, credential files, process environments, and cloud or CI tokens, then exfiltrated them. Both versions were removed; 1.26.0 is the last known clean release, and no patched version is listed.[1]

Treat any environment that installed either version as exposed—not merely repaired by uninstalling. Cached wheels and internal mirrors can preserve the payload.[1]

**2. AWS STS added runtime-scoped credentials.** *Shipped — GA, November 19.* `GetScopedCredentials` derives credentials from an existing temporary session while monotonically reducing permissions, duration, or both. The credentials preserve the caller’s identity, can be narrowed again, and each call is recorded in CloudTrail. AWS lists all commercial, GovCloud, European Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions.[3]

This gives parent agents a native way to issue task-specific credentials to subagents without creating a role for every delegation.

**3. GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol became generally available on Amazon Bedrock.** *Shipped — GA, November 17.* AWS positions Astra for difficult reasoning, research, coding, multimodal, and agentic work, with an Ultrafast mode; Sol targets recurring, higher-volume coding and multistep workflows. Both are accessible through supported Bedrock APIs and the console.[7]

The practical change is model choice inside existing AWS governance boundaries, not proof of better workload economics. Region, feature, inference-profile, and pricing details must be checked in Bedrock documentation before rollout.[7]

**4. AgentCore payments added AWS Marketplace purchasing.** *Shipped, November 19.* Agents can discover selected x402-enabled APIs, data, software, and content, pay per request in US dollars through the developer’s AWS bill, and avoid per-seller wallets or API keys. Controls include payment-session budgets, approved sellers, Private Marketplace policy, CloudTrail events, and Cost Explorer visibility.[4][5]

The first purchase creates a Marketplace agreement; the launch initially supports x402’s exact-price scheme. This turns tool acquisition into a governed runtime action, so spending authority now belongs in agent threat models.[5]

**5. MCP reference servers v2.5.0 patched eight more vulnerabilities.** *Open-sourced/published, November 18.* Fixed versions are `mcp-server-git` 2026.11.18, filesystem 2.4.0, and everything 2.3.1. The flaws covered Git maintenance hooks, lazy fetch and driver execution, out-of-tree index reads, filesystem symlink races, submodule configuration, and NAT64-assisted private-address access.[2]

Since the November 14 issue, this is a second consecutive security release. Operators must install exact versions: npm can rank older calendar-version packages above the newer semantic versions.[2]

**6. Gemini API introduced on-demand Tool Retrieval.** *Shipped — Preview, November 19.* Developers can defer full function or remote MCP schemas while leaving names and descriptions visible. The model requests a schema through `tool_search` only when needed; server-side retrieval stays within one API request, while client-side retrieval can enforce a private registry or permission filter.[6]

The design is relevant beyond Gemini: discovery, authorization, schema hydration, and invocation can be separate observable stages instead of putting every tool definition into every prompt.

## DevOps / platform impact

- **Security:** Inventory package versions and hashes across lockfiles, caches, mirrors, build logs, and deployed images; reinstalling a clean package does not revoke stolen credentials.[1]
- **IAM:** Derive least-privilege credentials per agent task and log the parent-to-child delegation chain rather than sharing a broad runtime role.[3]
- **Governance:** Treat agent purchasing as a privileged side effect with seller allowlists, session budgets, approval thresholds, billing alerts, and reconciliation.[4][5]
- **Deployment:** Pin exact MCP packages and model identifiers; package ordering and managed model catalogs can change behavior without an application-code diff.[2][7]
- **Architecture:** Keep tool discovery, permission filtering, schema loading, and execution distinct so large catalogs do not automatically become large prompt or authority surfaces.[6]

## Bring to work

**Compromised-package sweep — high effort.** Direct fit for any Python agent environment, including Bedrock-integrated services. Search SBOMs, caches, mirrors, CI artifacts, and images for 1.26.1/1.26.2 and the published wheel hashes; isolate affected systems and rotate every reachable credential.[1]

**Delegated-credential pilot — medium effort.** Direct AWS fit. Give one AgentCore or containerized agent a broad temporary session, derive task-scoped credentials for two subagents, and verify denied actions, duration limits, recursive narrowing, and CloudTrail reconstruction.[3]

**Model cost-per-success evaluation — medium effort.** Direct Bedrock fit. Compare Astra, Sol, and current defaults on 40 frozen tool-use tasks; measure completion, intervention, latency, tokens, and total cost rather than vendor positioning.[7]

**Tool-catalog boundary test — medium effort.** Transferable to AgentCore Gateway and MCP. Put 100 tools behind a searchable registry and compare eager schemas with deferred retrieval on token use, selection accuracy, permission leakage, latency, and auditability.[6]

## Watchouts

- The Microsoft package incident requires incident response and credential rotation, not only dependency rollback; internal mirrors may still serve the malicious wheels.[1]
- `GetScopedCredentials` can only narrow the caller’s temporary session. A broadly privileged parent remains a high-value target.[3]
- AgentCore Marketplace payments create real agreements and charges; separate the identity that sets budgets from the identity that spends them.[5]
- MCP v2.5.0 still documents a Windows filesystem-listing limitation and a Git confinement check not yet repeated after certain writes.[2]
- Gemini Tool Retrieval is preview, and Bedrock model claims require workload-specific validation of region, feature support, latency, and cost.[6][7]

## Sources

[1] https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-764m-3ppc-5m73 — Microsoft Agent Framework malicious PyPI packages
[2] https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/releases/tag/v2.5.0 — MCP reference servers v2.5.0
[3] https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/sts-getscopedcredentials — AWS STS GetScopedCredentials
[4] https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/marketplace-agentic-payments-agentcore — AWS Marketplace agentic payments with AgentCore
[5] https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/enable-ai-agents-to-pay-for-aws-marketplace-x402-products-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-payments — AgentCore payments x402 technical post
[6] https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-api-tool-retrieval — Gemini API Tool Retrieval
[7] https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/openai-gpt-6-2-astra-sol-amazon-bedrock — OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on Amazon Bedrock
